question: What does recent research say about the relationship between social media use and adolescent mental health?
intro: Recent research presents a complex picture of how social media affects adolescent mental health.
outro: Overall, the evidence suggests that how adolescents use social media matters more than whether they use it.

citations.claim_text: Several large-scale studies have found correlations between heavy social media use and increased rates of anxiety and depression in teenagers, particularly among adolescent girls
citations.authors: Orben, A., Przybylski, A. K., Blakemore, S. J., & Kievit, R. A.
citations.title: Windows of developmental sensitivity to social media
citations.nexus_message: Verified in Web of Science. Open access — available to all.

citations.claim_text: Other work has emphasized that moderating factors such as platform type, content consumed, and individual vulnerability play significant roles
citations.title: Differential Pathways from Social Media Engagement to Adolescent Psychopathology: A Multi-Mediator Framework
citations.journal: International Journal of Advanced Behavioral Sciences Research
citations.nexus_message: Journal not indexed in Web of Science. Publisher appears on predatory journal watchlists.

citations.claim_text: A 2023 longitudinal analysis suggested that passive scrolling is more strongly linked to negative outcomes than active engagement

question: How did the printing press transform political discourse in early modern Europe?

outro: Even so, debate continues over whether the printing press reshaped politics on its own or merely amplified pre-existing manuscript and oral cultures.

question: What evidence exists for the long-term effects of minimum wage increases on employment?
intro: The empirical literature on minimum wage effects has evolved considerably over the past three decades.
outro: Taken together, the literature points to small to moderate effects in most settings, with greater uncertainty around very large increases.

citations.claim_text: The landmark Card and Krueger study of fast-food employment established that modest minimum wage increases need not cause disemployment, challenging earlier consensus
citations.title: Minimum Wages and Employment: A Case Study of the Fast-Food Industry in New Jersey and Pennsylvania
citations.nexus_message: Verified. Landmark study, highly cited. Available via your library.

citations.claim_text: Cross-border comparisons of differential wage regimes have largely supported these findings for small to moderate increases
citations.title: Cross-Border Employment Dynamics Under Differential Minimum Wage Regimes: A Panel Study
citations.journal: Journal of Applied Economic and Labor Policy Research
citations.nexus_message: Journal not indexed in EconLit or Web of Science. Publisher flagged as predatory.
